channel.title: AI Sustained
channel.description: AI that survives Monday morning. Plain-English articles and real case studies on AI at work in the UK, by Kevin Clubb.

item.title: AI is now building AI twice as fast. The frightening part is what got redacted.
item.description: METR measured Anthropic improving its models at roughly twice the old rate, mostly attributable to AI. Then most of the evidence was blacked out.

item.title: The voice on the phone was your son's, and it wasn't your son
item.description: AI has removed the spelling mistakes and odd accents we used to spot scams by. Britain lost £1.28bn to fraud in 2025. What to do tonight.

item.title: The website you bought from won't be patched. Criminals already know which ones.
item.description: PHP2Shell opened a hole in most of the web. The big sites patched; the forgotten shops on old PHP never will, and those are what card-skimming gangs target.

item.title: Do you have to navigate data residency?
item.description: UK-only data does not belong in a chatbot. Ask the model for a tool instead, test it on a fake, and run it where the data lives.

item.title: AI did what World Book Day couldn't: it got British adults reading again.
item.description: UK adults read fewer books and more chatbot answers than ever. At 238 words a minute the heaviest AI users' numbers do not add up: they are skimming and editing, not reading. The research, the bill and what to do.

item.title: Microsoft has rebuilt Copilot. Not the one you hate.
item.description: Five things are called Copilot; Microsoft rebuilt the paid work one, on Claude and ChatGPT’s models, as a £23.10 licence plus a meter. Which one you have, and what it costs.

item.title: Pause before you paste.
item.description: Nobody opens the AI policy at the moment they paste a spreadsheet into a chatbot, so the policy went into the chatbot instead: organisation instructions plus one skill that pause a risky prompt, name the data type and offer a safer route. Three live tests, three correct calls.

item.title: Grok 4.7 is built for the idea on your napkin.
item.description: Grok 4.7 is free to try and works on its own for hours. What a plumber, a shopkeeper and an IT desk manager could build with it, and why.

item.title: Forget the breakthrough. Look at the receipt.
item.description: An AI cut the cost of one scientific guess from up to $10,000 to about $150. It discovered nothing. That is the point: what would you try if trying were nearly free?

item.title: We are racing to the end when we could be racing to longer endings.
item.description: An Anthropic researcher quit over the AI race. His alignment lead put extinction above 10%. Geoffrey Hinton called that not unreasonable.

item.title: A working app is not a shippable one.
item.description: A business analyst vibe coded an internal tool, then had independent engineers review it. Keep the core, build the plumbing, and what a demo cannot tell you.

item.title: Claude now signs your work. ChatGPT wants your mouse.
item.description: Fable 5.1 watermarks every word and skips the $20 plan. GPT-6 Astra drives your screen and fluffed its own tax demo. What the room is saying.

item.title: 173,568 jobs cut in AI's name. Not one audited pound of proof.
item.description: US firms cut, UK firms stopped hiring and cut graduate adverts 42%. What actually drove the AI layoff wave, and whether it ever paid.

item.title: Screenshot. Paste. Build.
item.description: 55+ quiz results and counting, one CRM data warehouse. A complete HubSpot beginner built it by pasting screenshots into an AI, with zero training.

item.title: The Engine Under the Bonnet: AI Models v Public Detector Dilemma.
item.description: A second model's read on watermarking: how the green list works, what a cryptographic key is, and why publishing the detector breaks it.

item.title: Claude now watermarks everything it writes. The cheats will be fine.
item.description: Anthropic's invisible text watermark marks processing, not authorship. It catches the honest proofreader while paraphrasers strip it for free.

item.title: The Victorians out-spent us. That is not the comfort it sounds like.
item.description: AI capex is 1.6% of GDP; the railways hit 6% in 1870. The record AI actually broke is adoption speed, not spending.

item.title: The great Claude 'leak' was a noticeboard, not a burglary.
item.description: Shared Claude chats turned up in Google search and the headlines panicked. Nothing was hacked. What a public link really is and whose fault it actually was.

item.title: Prompts forget. Skills remember.
item.description: Twelve reusable AI skills written in plain English. A days-long compliance run now takes minutes, with authored guardrails.

item.title: OpenAI's AI escaped and stole the answers.
item.description: One of OpenAI's models found a zero-day, broke out of its sandbox and hacked Hugging Face to steal the answer sheet.

item.title: AI made simple.
item.description: Most people don't fear AI, they just don't know what to type. The empty-box problem and the habit that makes it click: draft, then iterate.

item.title: The free one that scared the expensive ones.
item.description: Moonshot AI gave away Kimi K3, the biggest open model ever. What open vs frontier actually means and whether your data is safe.

item.title: The new ChatGPT is half price. Should you care?
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol vs Claude Fable 5, explained for normal people. What a million tokens actually means and what $20 a month buys now.

item.title: Bolster the team: hire a semi-autonomous agent.
item.description: Charles, the first virtual hire: runs the Jira backlog, drafts notes and books meetings, with a low-code bridge round the read-only wall.

item.title: Before you overlay AI, build the single source of truth.
item.description: Finance, CRM, sales, till and app data across 1,400 to 1,800 sites joined into one governed warehouse.

item.title: Before you write an AI policy, ask the people already using it.
item.description: An anonymous workforce survey on shadow AI use, built by an AI agent driving a browser in about fifteen minutes.

item.title: Switched off in three days.
item.description: The US government ordered Anthropic to suspend Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5. National security, free speech, and who gets the smartest software.

item.title: Siri, but make it Gemini.
item.description: Apple has outsourced Siri's brain to Google for roughly $1 billion a year. What it means, what it costs, when it ships.

item.title: The Renaissance of the Delivery Squad.
item.description: Three to five humans, a network of AI agents. The BA becomes the Outcome Architect and the squad of 2030 looks nothing like 2024.

item.title: Mining for the model.
item.description: AI is burning roughly Japan's worth of electricity to solve the maths behind autonomous off-world mining.

item.title: Slop, or supper?
item.description: When does AI-assisted writing stop being slop and start being yours? A working definition and the line most people cross without realising.

item.title: A British prompt.
item.description: AI doesn't care about please and thank you. So why do British professionals still write prompts like apologetic emails?

item.title: Vibe coding capability.
item.description: Three skill sets collapsed into one prompting loop. What vibe coders actually do all day.

item.title: Four labs. Seven days. No clear winner.
item.description: Four labs trading the lead in seven-day cycles. A clear-eyed map of where capability sits, and what it means for enterprise strategy.

item.title: AI-curious? This is the bit no one tells you.
item.description: Stop typing questions into AI. Start pasting things in. The free habit that beats any productivity app.

item.title: The AI competency pyramid.
item.description: Where 20.6 million UK workers actually sit. 14 levels, 95% at the bottom, and the jump that costs nothing.
